name: Delfina Ochoa
equipment: Leather duster, tan, cut long for riding, with a torn pocket where a rattlesnake once was
Army revolver (Colt single-action, .45), 6 rounds loaded, in a cross-draw holster her father tooled
Bowie knife in a boot sheath
Horse: Tía, a grey sorrel mare, short-coupled and bad-tempered, the fastest horse on the creek over a quarter mile
Saddle, bridle, saddlebags, bedroll and a slicker
The Association's printed reward notice: FERGUS MALLORY, HORSE THIEF, $500, folded small
A Platte River Stock Growers' Association inspector's commission, issued in Cheyenne in April, which she has not yet decided to be proud of
Field glasses in a leather case, and a set of manacles she has used more often than her gun
A tin of coffee, a twist of tobacco she does not smoke but trades, and a rosary that was her mother's
features: Both Sides of the River (Borderlands origin: speaks English and Spanish natively, knows the fords, trails and towns on both sides of the border, and has advantage on Persuasion and Insight checks with border people of either side)

Quick Draw (Gunslinger: advantage on initiative rolls and on the draw in a showdown; when she rolls initiative and isn't surprised she draws a Sidearm as part of the roll, and drawing or holstering a Sidearm never costs her an interaction)

Gun Hand: Steady Hand (Gunslinger: once on each of her turns, when she rolls a 1 on a damage die for a Sidearm single shot, she can reroll that die and must use the new roll; this does not change the attack bonus or damage on her sheet)

Fan the Hammer (Gunslinger, 2nd level: when she fans a single-action revolver she can fan up to 4 rounds in one action instead of 3, and the first of those attacks is made without disadvantage; fanned shots add no ability modifier to damage)

Paper on Him (Bounty Hunter background: sheriffs, marshals and express agents know her as someone who brings them in, and tell her who is wanted, for what, for how much, and where they were last seen; she knows who pays rewards honestly; outlaws and their kin know her face too)

personality.traits: I talk very little and laugh at the wrong moments. I sit with my back to a wall and my right hand free. I am polite to everyone until they give me a reason, and then I am polite to them in Spanish, which is worse.
personality.ideals: A price on a man's head is a contract, not a licence. I bring them in alive when I can, and I never shoot a man for a piece of paper somebody else wrote.
personality.bonds: My cousin Joe Pruneda, who breaks horses for Calvin Booker on the creek and is on the Association's list. And my father's saddle, which I will be buried in.
personality.flaws: I took the Association's money before I asked what it was for. I am proud, and when I am wrong I would rather be shot than say so.

appearance: A compact, sun-dark woman of twenty-eight with black hair in a single braid down her back, a narrow face, a scar through her left eyebrow and very steady brown eyes. She wears a man's flat-crowned hat, a tan duster, a blue cotton shirt and her father's spurs. She stands very still, and when she moves it is all at once.
backstory: Delfina Ochoa was born on a ranch outside Laredo, on the Texas side of the Rio Grande, the daughter of a vaquero who taught Anglo trail bosses how to handle longhorns and was paid half what they were. She learned to ride before she could walk and to shoot before she could read, and when her father was killed by horse thieves in 1879 she went after them, alone, and brought two of them back to the sheriff in Laredo across their saddles. The sheriff paid her the reward and told her not to do it again. She has done it ever since, from the Nueces to the Platte, and she is good at it, and nobody has ever paid her what they would have paid a man. In April 1886 she rode north to Wyoming after the Association's $500 reward for a horse thief named Fergus Mallory, and in Cheyenne the Association's secretary offered her a stock inspector's commission and sixty dollars a month to go to Bitter Creek with seven other hired guns. She took it. On the Rawlins stage she found out that the dead list includes her cousin Joe, whom she has not seen in five years. On the first day in Gilead, a homesteader is found hanged with the Association's name on a sign, and Delfina Ochoa, who has never in her life shot a man for a piece of paper, is wearing the Association's commission in her pocket. (Suggested employer: the Company. Hooks into the grange: her cousin Joe Pruneda, and the bounty on Fergus Mallory, who is not what the poster says.)
